title: ALMA-IMF. XII. Point-process mapping of 15 massive protoclusters
question: Measure luminosity, mass, column density and dust temperature of the 15 ALMA-IMF protoclusters at 2.5 arcsec resolution with PPMAP SED fitting, then extract luminosity peaks and compare luminosity-to-mass ratios with evolutionary stage and tracks

recipe.method: Repair or drop saturated Herschel maps, build PSFs for all instruments, apply Herschel colour corrections, and set per-map errors; use free-free-subtracted and native Band 6 versions
key_parameters: Maps with 25% or more saturated area removed (11 of 124 images); maps with less than 25% saturated were interpolated
25 of 124 images interpolated, median 6 pixels per image
Herschel PSFs replaced by versions on 2048 x 2048 frames
Per-map error = MAD of empty areas plus flux-calibration error times sky background
Gaussian synthetic beams for SABOCA, LABOCA and ALMA
assumptions: Herschel colour corrections assume a modified blackbody with beta = 2
Free-free subtraction assumes electron temperature of 7000 K and region-dependent helium abundance

recipe.goal: Run PPMAP SED fitting (Run1 and Run2)
recipe.method: Multi-resolution Bayesian SED fitting of 70 um to 1.3 mm maps with PPMAP; Run1 uses free-free-subtracted Band 6 for column density and temperature, Run2 uses native Band 6 for luminosity
key_parameters: 8 MBB components, 10-50 K
Opacity index fixed to beta = 1.8
1.25'' pixels, 2.5'' synthetic resolution
Reference opacity kappa_300 = 0.1 cm2/g
Maximum 10 000 iterations
Dilution eta = 0 (internal default N_prior/N_states)
Cells of 60 px, overlap 40 px (50 px in some cases giving 7x7 mosaics)
High-pass option on, subtracting a constant background from model images at ground-based wavelengths
Temperature range lowered per region after a first run (example G012.80: 21-39 K)
assumptions: Dust emission optically thin at all wavelengths
Gas-to-dust mass ratio of 100 (kappa_300 defined w.r.t. total mass)
X_H = 0.7, X_H2 = 1, Z_D = 0.01 for the H2 column density

recipe.goal: Correct dust temperature for optical depth
recipe.method: Build a correction table from PPMAP runs on synthetic uniform-slab observations, extrapolate it with cubic splines and apply it a posteriori to each pixel
key_parameters: Grid of model sources over temperature, optical depth, size and measurement error
Synthetic flux maps between 70 um and 3 mm
Cubic-spline extrapolation beyond the original table limits
assumptions: Simplified slab model; column density not changed by the correction

recipe.goal: Suppress ring artifacts and resample products
recipe.method: Convolve with a 1 pixel Gaussian, replace pixels where the relative change is above a threshold and Band 6 is at noise level, then resample to 3 pixels per beam
key_parameters: Relative-difference threshold t = 0.05
Pixels with significant Band 6 signal left unchanged
Resampling from 2 to 3 pixels per beam; reproject_exact on temperature maps

recipe.goal: Derive bolometric luminosity, mass and L/M per footprint
recipe.method: Compute L_MBB from the Run2 model; add Spitzer and SOFIA near/mid-infrared by piecewise cubic Hermite interpolation to get L_bol (3.6 um to 1.3 mm); derive gas mass from Run1 column density; integrate in the ALMA mosaic and ATLASGAL footprints
key_parameters: L_bol integrated from 3.6 um to 1.3 mm
Footprints: ALMA 12 m array mosaic primary-beam response, and ATLASGAL source footprints
assumptions: Distances to the regions taken from the ALMA-IMF paper I

recipe.method: Re-run PPMAP with modified inputs (saturation, free-free, noise estimator, beta, artifacts, pointing shifts), take map differences, add the PPMAP fit errors and combine in quadrature
key_parameters: beta = 1.8 +/- 0.2 for the opacity-index error
Relative Herschel pointing shifts of 1'' and 2.5''
Three noise estimate methods compared
assumptions: Total uncertainties exclude the kappa_300 uncertainty and the optically thin bias

recipe.method: Aperture photometry of the PPMAP luminosity and column density maps in the same apertures as Koenig et al., with distance correction, then compare luminosity and mass
key_parameters: Comparison on a subset of regions observed by both studies (stated as 10)
assumptions: Koenig et al. use a two-temperature MBB over 8-870 um

recipe.goal: Column density PDFs and N2H+ comparison
recipe.method: Build the mean column density PDF, fit a lognormal plus power-law tail in G012.80, and compare maps visually with N2H+ J=1-0 integrated emission

recipe.goal: Map L/M and extract luminosity peaks with getsf
recipe.method: Pixel-by-pixel L/M PDFs by evolutionary stage, then getsf on the resampled Run2 luminosity maps with Run1 column density as auxiliary image to get masses, giving a source catalog
key_parameters: Luminosity maps resampled to three pixels per beam
Maximum source size 5'' (twice the PPMAP beam)
Luminosity-map clustering threshold log(L/M) = 1.8 (G012.80 illustration)
assumptions: Peaks with no massive counterpart interpreted as diffuse areas heated by evolved protostars or HII regions

recipe.goal: Compare source L/M with evolutionary tracks
recipe.method: Place the catalog sources in the M-Lbol diagram and compare with accretion evolutionary tracks
assumptions: Massive sources above the 50 Msun track are unresolved clusters of cores/protostars
